patients.summary: Former construction laborer on Medicaid with severe alcohol use disorder and compensated alcoholic cirrhosis who joins the practice in August 2024. Three withdrawal-delirium admissions in eleven months lead to acamprosate and an outpatient addiction program, after which he reports abstinence.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer his primary care here. Says his old office is too far now that he is living in Easthampton and he has no car most days. Medicaid card on file, plan is accepted. His sister may drive him to appointments. Offered the 8/20 new patient slot at 9:00, he took it. Records release form emailed for his former PCP office. Reminded him to bring all pill bottles.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53M new to me, transferring from a prior primary care office (records requested). Came alone today.

He is straightforward about drinking: roughly a fifth of vodka a day for about fifteen years. Has tried to quit on his own several times; each time he got shaky and sweaty and went back to it within a day or two. Never been through a detox unit or a program. Not interested in cutting down right now, though he says he knows where it is heading - his father drank, had cirrhosis, and died at 61. Last drink was last night.

Known problems per patient and pill bottles: alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis (told by the old office a few years ago, no specialist), hypertension, thiamine deficiency, depression, reflux. Appendix out at 22. No other surgery.

Meds: thiamine 100 daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, a multivitamin, omeprazole 20 daily, amlodipine 5 daily. Says he takes them most days. NKDA.

Family: father as above. Mother has high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. One sister, who has anxiety; she is the person he leans on.

Social: lives alone in an apartment in town. Worked construction as a laborer for years, out of work now. Smokes a pack a day, has since his early twenties, ~30 pack-years. No other drugs.

Mood: low on and off for years, given a depression diagnosis at the old office. Sleep is broken, energy poor. Denies any thoughts of harming himself. PHQ-9 9. Does not want an antidepressant, 'I've got enough pills.' AUDIT-C 12.

ROS: no jaundice he has noticed, no belly swelling, no black stools or vomiting blood, no confusion. Heartburn controlled on omeprazole.

Exam: thin, alert, smells of tobacco. BP 134/84. Wt 74 kg, ht 178 cm. Anicteric. No asterixis, no tremor at rest today. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites, liver edge not felt, healed RLQ scar. No spider angiomata seen, no palmar erythema. No leg swelling. Oriented, fluent, appropriate.

A/P
1. Severe alcohol use disorder. Long talk about the risks, including withdrawal if he stops abruptly - he should call us or go to the ED if he gets confused, sees things, or shakes badly. He is not ready for treatment; door is open.
2. Alcoholic cirrhosis, never seen hepatology. CMP, GGT, CBC, PT/INR today. Referring to hepatology for staging and surveillance. Hep B surface Ag/Ab, hep C, HIV today. Starting hep A and hep B series today along with PCV20.
3. HTN at goal on amlodipine 5. Continue.
4. Thiamine deficiency - continue thiamine, folate, MVI.
5. Depression, mild by PHQ. Declines medication. Will recheck at visits.
6. GERD - continue omeprazole.
7. Tobacco - advised to quit, not ready, declines nicotine replacement. Qualifies for lung screening; low-dose CT ordered.
8. Colon screening never done - FIT kit given.

Return in about 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kevin, your blood work from Tuesday is back. Your liver enzymes (AST 72, ALT 50, GGT 150) are elevated in the pattern we see with heavy alcohol use, which fits what we talked about. Bilirubin 1.2 is borderline. Blood clotting test, blood counts, kidneys and cholesterol are fine, magnesium is at the low end of normal (1.8). Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests are all negative - you are not immune to hepatitis B, which is why we started that vaccine. The hepatology office should call you to set up a visit. Second hep B shot is due in about 4 weeks; the front desk can book a nurse visit.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Received by fax, 22 pages: office notes 2019 to 2024 from his previous primary care practice.

Problem list as they kept it: alcohol dependence, alcoholic cirrhosis, hypertension, thiamine deficiency, major depression, GERD. Past surgical: appendectomy.
Medications: thiamine 100 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, multivitamin daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Immunizations: Tdap 2019. No pneumococcal or hepatitis vaccines on record.
Notes repeatedly document heavy daily alcohol use with counseling given and declined. Visits were irregular, often a year apart.

Abstracted to chart; nothing new. Original in media tab.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for second dose of the two-dose hep B series. No problems after the first one. Given IM left deltoid, lot recorded. Tolerated. Hep B series now complete. Hep A #2 due February. He has not returned the FIT kit yet - reminded him, says it is on his kitchen table.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: MA
documents.body: FIT negative. Per PCP, repeat in one year. Letter mailed to patient.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (baseline)
Indication: Current smoker, 30 pack-years, age 53. Asymptomatic.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Heart size normal; no pericardial effusion. No enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes. The visualized upper abdomen is limited by technique. No aggressive osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Baseline lung screening CT negative, Lung-RADS 1. Repeat next September. Portal note sent; also used it as another nudge to quit smoking.

documents.title: Hepatology consultation
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Outside hepatology group - new patient consultation, seen 10/8/2024. Letter to the referring primary care physician.

Thank you for sending this 53-year-old man with a known diagnosis of alcohol-related cirrhosis made at his previous practice, never previously seen by a liver specialist. He drinks roughly 750 mL of vodka daily and smokes a pack per day. He has had no jaundice, ascites, encephalopathy or GI bleeding. Other history: hypertension, reflux, depression, thiamine deficiency, remote appendectomy. Medications: thiamine, folic acid, multivitamin, omeprazole 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg. No known drug allergies.

On examination he was alert without asterixis, anicteric, abdomen soft without fluid wave or splenomegaly.

Your recent labs: AST 72, ALT 50, bilirubin 1.2, albumin and INR normal, platelets normal, GGT 150. Viral hepatitis screen negative; I see hepatitis A and B vaccination is underway, which I appreciate.

Impression: compensated alcohol-related cirrhosis, Child-Pugh class A.

Recommendations:
1. Complete abstinence is the single most important thing for his liver. We discussed this directly.
2. Liver ultrasound now for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance and every 6 months thereafter.
3. Screening upper endoscopy for varices - scheduled with our endoscopy unit.
4. Avoid NSAIDs; acetaminophen no more than 2 g daily.
5. Follow-up here in about 6 to 8 months.

Allergies: NKDA.

reports.text:
ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN, COMPLETE
Indication: Alcohol-related cirrhosis; hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance.
Comparison: None available.
Liver: Coarsened echotexture with a nodular surface contour, consistent with cirrhosis. No focal hepatic lesion. Main portal vein patent with normal direction of flow on color imaging.
Gallbladder: No stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct 4 mm.
Pancreas: Visualized portions unremarkable.
Spleen: 10.8 cm, normal in size.
Kidneys: Normal size and echogenicity bilaterally; no hydronephrosis.
Aorta: Normal caliber where seen.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhotic liver morphology without focal lesion. No ascites. Normal spleen size. Patent portal vein.

documents.title: Liver ultrasound received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hepatology's surveillance US: cirrhotic liver, no mass, no ascites, spleen normal. They will repeat in 6 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal shots. Agreed to start the shingles series too after the PCP's suggestion at intake. Influenza L deltoid, COVID R deltoid, Shingrix R deltoid lower site. Warned the shingles shot can make him feel achy for a day or two. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Shingrix #2 in 2 to 6 months - will pair with hep A #2 in February.

documents.title: Upper endoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside endoscopy unit, procedure date 11/14/2024. Copy to primary care.

Procedure: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy.
Indication: Screening for esophageal varices in compensated alcohol-related cirrhosis.
Sedation: Monitored anesthesia care. Tolerated well.
Allergies: NKDA.

Findings:
Esophagus: Normal mucosa throughout. No varices. No esophagitis. Z-line regular.
Stomach: Normal; no portal hypertensive gastropathy, no gastric varices.
Duodenum: Normal to the second portion.
No biopsies taken.

Impression: Normal EGD. No esophageal or gastric varices. Reflux without esophagitis on current PPI.

Plan: No beta-blocker indicated. Repeat variceal screening per hepatology, typically in 2 to 3 years if he continues to drink, sooner if anything changes. Continue omeprazole.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED physician record, visit 12/3/2024. Received with the discharge summary.

CC: seeing things, agitated.

HPI: 53 y/o man brought in by his sister, who says since this morning he has been seeing things that aren't there and can't settle. He drinks about a fifth of vodka every day and says his last drink was roughly 18 hours ago. Has tried to stop before. PMH: alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis, HTN, thiamine deficiency, depression, GERD. PSH: appendectomy age 22. Home meds: thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, MVI, omeprazole 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, all daily. Allergies: NKDA. Smokes 1 ppd x 30 years.

Triage: BP 160/100, HR 110, RR 22, T 37.8 C.

Exam: Anxious, shaking, sweating. Pupils dilated. Reflexes brisk throughout. Knows who he is, where he is and the date, but keeps glancing around the room and responding to things that aren't there. No focal neuro deficit.

Labs: Na 140, K 4.0, Cl 100, BUN 18, Cr 1.1, glucose 90, Mg 1.8, Ca 9.2. AST 72, ALT 50, GGT 150. MCV 96.

ED course: IV thiamine given before any dextrose. Lorazepam IV in repeated doses by withdrawal scale. Magnesium sulfate IV. Fluids.

Impression: Alcohol withdrawal delirium.
Disposition: Admitted to the medical floor for ongoing withdrawal management.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service. Admitted 12/3/2024, discharged 12/6/2024.

Principal diagnosis: Alcohol withdrawal delirium.
Other: Severe alcohol use disorder; alcoholic cirrhosis, compensated; hypertension; thiamine deficiency; major depressive disorder; GERD.

Course: Admitted from the ED with hallucinations, tremor and autonomic hyperactivity about 18 hours after his last drink. Managed with symptom-triggered IV lorazepam on a withdrawal protocol, high-dose IV thiamine for 3 days, IV fluids and magnesium replacement. Hallucinations cleared by the second hospital day and he needed no further lorazepam after the morning of 12/5. No seizures. Blood pressure settled back on amlodipine as withdrawal resolved. Addiction consult offered; he declined residential treatment and took a list of outpatient resources.

Discharge meds (unchanged from home): thiamine 100 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, multivitamin daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily. No benzodiazepines prescribed at discharge.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: Primary care within one week.

documents.title: Call from patient's sister
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sister called (listed as his emergency contact). Kevin was taken to the ED yesterday after he stopped drinking and started seeing things; he was admitted. She wanted us to know. She sounded worried - says she has been through this kind of thing with their father. Explained we will get the records and want to see him within a week of discharge. She will call when he's out. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Sister drove him and sat in.

Admitted 12/3 to 12/6 for alcohol withdrawal delirium after stopping abruptly - discharge summary reviewed. He remembers little of the first day. Hallucinations gone. Sleep poor. He started drinking again two days after he got home, 'less than before', which by his description is still most of a bottle. No seizures, no falls, no vomiting blood, no black stools.

Meds unchanged: thiamine, folic acid, MVI, omeprazole 20, amlodipine 5.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Alert, calm, no tremor today, no asterixis. Anicteric. Abdomen soft, no fluid. Normal gait.

A/P
- Alcohol withdrawal delirium, resolved. He now knows what stopping cold can do. Very clear advice: do not stop suddenly on his own; if he wants to stop, call us first so it is done safely, or go to the ED. Sister heard this too.
- AUD severe - still not ready for a program. Gave him the hospital's resource list back and the number for the regional recovery line.
- Cirrhosis - CMP and Mg today. Hepatology follow-up is set for spring.
- HTN fine.
- Recheck in about 2 months.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request from his pharmacy for amlodipine 5 mg and omeprazole 20 mg, 90-day supplies. Last visit 12/11, on current med list. Sent per protocol, 1 refill each. Pharmacy asked whether thiamine/folate/MVI can be billed to his plan - they are covered as prescriptions; new scripts sent for all three so his copay goes away.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up. Doing about the same. Drinking daily, says he hasn't tried to stop since December 'because of what happened.' Still a pack a day. Mood flat but he is getting out to his sister's for dinner most Sundays. No confusion, no belly swelling, no bleeding. Heartburn quiet.

Exam: BP and weight as charted - pressure is fine on amlodipine. No tremor. Anicteric, abdomen soft, no ascites. No edema.

Plan:
- AUD: we talked again about treatment, including medication-assisted options. He wants to think about it.
- Cirrhosis: CMP, CBC, INR, GGT today. Hepatology ultrasound due in May.
- Hep A #2 and Shingrix #2 given today - both series complete.
- Smoking: not ready.
- HTN: amlodipine 5, no change.
Back in 3 months.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate about 120. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal for rate. No ST elevation or depression. No arrhythmia.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, date of service 4/1/2025, evening.

Chief complaint: confused and agitated, seeing and feeling bugs.

History (from sister, patient unable to give a reliable account): 54-year-old man with alcohol use disorder, seen in this ED in December 2024 for withdrawal delirium. She says he has gone 72 hours without a drink, which is not like him. Now restless, not making sense, says bugs are crawling on the walls and on him.
PMH per records: AUD, alcoholic cirrhosis, HTN, thiamine deficiency, MDD, GERD; appendectomy. Meds: thiamine, folic acid, multivitamin, omeprazole 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg. Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: T 39.2 C (102.5 F), BP 175/95, HR 120.
Exam: Drenched in sweat, coarse tremor, jumps at any noise or touch. Disoriented. Neck supple. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs: Na 140, K 3.9, Cl 100, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, glucose 150, Mg 1.8. AST 72, ALT 50, alk phos 85, total bilirubin 1.2.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, nothing else.

Treatment: IV thiamine, IV lorazepam in escalating doses per protocol, IV fluids, magnesium. Blood cultures, urinalysis and chest film sent for the fever.

Assessment: Delirium tremens. Fever, tachycardia and hyperglycemia most consistent with withdrawal; infection being excluded.
Disposition: ICU.

reports.text:
PORTABLE AP CHEST
Indication: Fever, delirium.
Lungs are clear without focal consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette within normal limits. No acute bony abnormality.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 4/2/2025 (from ED 4/1), discharged 4/7/2025.

Diagnoses: Delirium tremens. Stress hyperglycemia. Sinus tachycardia due to alcohol withdrawal. Background: severe alcohol use disorder, compensated alcoholic cirrhosis, hypertension, thiamine deficiency, MDD, GERD.

Hospital course: Three days in the medical ICU on a symptom-triggered lorazepam protocol, which needed high doses on day 1 and tapered off by day 3. High-dose IV thiamine, IV fluids, magnesium repletion. Fever workup unrevealing: portable chest film clear, urinalysis negative, blood cultures no growth at 5 days; fever resolved within 48 hours as withdrawal settled. Glucose 150 on arrival attributed to stress; no diabetes history. Transferred to the floor on day 4, oriented, eating, walking. Social work met with him and his sister; he declined residential treatment.

Discharge medications (no changes): thiamine 100 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, multivitamin daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily. No sedatives at discharge.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 7 days. Consider hemoglobin A1c as an outpatient.

documents.title: Call from sister
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sister called - Kevin is in the ICU again since last night, the same withdrawal problem but worse, he had a fever. She is not sure why he stopped this time. She is exhausted. Gave her our number for when he's discharged and told her the hospital will send records. Offered her the PCP's message line if she has questions. Routed to PCP to flag for TCM visit.

documents.title: Post-ICU visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 3 days after discharge from his second withdrawal admission, this time ICU with DTs (4/1 to 4/7). Records reviewed: fever workup negative, glucose 150 called stress.

He says he quit because he 'wanted to see if he could', no plan, no warning to anyone. Back to drinking since Tuesday, though he says less. Shaky in the mornings. Sister with him again, upset.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Fine tremor of the hands, oriented, no asterixis, no jaundice. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft without fluid.

A/P
- DTs, resolved. Second withdrawal admission in four months; this one more severe. Explained that each episode tends to be worse than the last. He listened.
- Severe AUD: offered referral to an outpatient addiction program and discussed medication to reduce cravings. He is 'not there yet'. Will keep asking.
- Stress hyperglycemia in hospital - BMP today; A1c at his physical.
- Cirrhosis - US in May per hepatology.
- Same meds. Return in 2 to 3 months.

reports.text:
ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN
Indication: Cirrhosis, 6-month HCC surveillance.
Comparison: 10/17/2024.
Liver: Coarse, heterogeneous echotexture with mildly nodular contour, unchanged. No discrete hepatic mass. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow.
Gallbladder: Normal, no stones.
Bile ducts: Not dilated.
Spleen: 11.0 cm.
Kidneys: Unremarkable.
No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Stable cirrhotic morphology. No focal liver lesion. No ascites. Spleen normal in size.

documents.title: Surveillance US
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Surveillance ultrasound unchanged, no lesion, no ascites. Copy to hepatology on file.

documents.title: Hepatology follow-up
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Outside hepatology group, follow-up visit 6/10/2025.

Since we met he has had two admissions for complicated alcohol withdrawal (December and April), the second in the ICU. He continues to drink daily. No ascites, jaundice, confusion or bleeding.

Medications: thiamine, folic acid, multivitamin, omeprazole 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg. NKDA.
Exam: Anicteric. No asterixis. Abdomen soft, no shifting dullness.
Data: May ultrasound without focal lesion or ascites. Endoscopy in November without varices. February labs: AST around 70, ALT around 50, bilirubin 1.3, normal INR and albumin, platelets normal.

Assessment: Compensated alcohol-related cirrhosis, Child-Pugh A, with ongoing heavy drinking.
Plan: I told him plainly that continued drinking is the main threat to his liver and that withdrawal itself is now dangerous for him; any attempt to stop should be medically supervised. I support whatever addiction treatment his primary care team can arrange; acamprosate would be my preference over naltrexone given his liver. Ultrasound again in 6 months. Return in 6 to 8 months.

documents.title: Missed visit outreach
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called about yesterday's missed 3 pm visit. He said his ride fell through and he forgot to call. Offered a video visit so he doesn't need transport; booked 8/5 at 10:30. Sent the video link instructions to his email.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from his apartment; verified name and DOB. Sister not present.

He is drinking about the same, every day. No attempts to stop since April. Mood 'so-so'; sleeps poorly, no thoughts of self-harm. I raised an antidepressant again and he still prefers not to. He did read the hepatology letter and knows the specialist suggested a craving medication - says maybe in the fall.

No jaundice he's noticed, no swelling, no confusion, no bleeding. Taking his meds.

Assessment and plan:
- Severe AUD, precontemplative to contemplative. Reviewed the safe-stopping plan again: call us first, do not stop cold.
- MDD, mild symptoms, declines medication.
- Cirrhosis compensated. Labs and physical in September.
- HTN - no home cuff; will check in person.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 54M.

Interval: two withdrawal admissions (12/2024 withdrawal delirium, 4/2025 DTs with ICU stay). Still drinking a fifth a day. Smokes 1 ppd. Hepatology following cirrhosis - compensated, no varices on last year's EGD, ultrasounds clean.

PHQ-9 8, no SI. AUDIT-C 12.
ROS otherwise negative: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no change in bowels, no blood in stool, no urinary symptoms, no weight loss.

Meds: thiamine 100, folic acid 1, MVI, omeprazole 20, amlodipine 5. NKDA.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Thin, alert. HEENT unremarkable, dentition fair. Neck supple, no nodes, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites, no organomegaly palpable. No spider angiomas. Skin warm and dry. Extremities without edema. Neuro: alert and oriented, no tremor, no asterixis, gait steady.

Assessment/plan:
- Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, INR, GGT, Mg, and A1c (hyperglycemia in the hospital in April). FIT kit given. Repeat low-dose CT ordered. Flu and COVID boosters when they arrive next month. Vaccine series otherwise done (PCV20, hep A, hep B, Shingrix).
- Severe AUD: same conversation; he says he is 'thinking about the medicine.' Reminded him about the safe-stopping plan.
- Cirrhosis, HTN, GERD, thiamine deficiency, MDD: stable, no changes.
- Tobacco: advised to quit; declines patch or other aids.
Follow-up in 3 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kevin - labs from your physical are back. A1c 5.4, so no sign of diabetes; the high sugar in April was from the stress of being so sick. Liver enzymes are about where they have been, which tells me the liver is still under strain from alcohol. Cholesterol, blood counts, clotting and kidney numbers all fine. Don't forget the stool card and the CT on the 23rd.

Regional hospital emergency department. Seen Sunday 11/2/2025 early afternoon.

Presenting problem: odd behavior, agitation, shaking, heavy sweating.

History: Third visit to this department in 11 months for the same pattern (December 2024 withdrawal delirium, April 2025 DTs requiring ICU). His sister reports he stopped drinking three days ago and has been acting strangely since. She says he has tried to stop many times over the years, and this looks just like the last two times. Patient is disoriented to time and place and describes small animals moving around the room.
Known history: alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis, HTN, thiamine deficiency, MDD, GERD; appendectomy. Medications: thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, MVI, omeprazole 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg daily. NKDA.

Vitals on arrival: BP 160/100, HR 120, T 38.9 C (102 F), RR 22.
Exam: Anxious, in constant motion, pupils dilated, coarse tremor of both hands with arms outstretched. Diaphoretic. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Results: Na 140, K 3.9, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, glucose 150, Mg 1.8, phos 2.5, Ca 9.2. AST 72, ALT 50, total bilirubin 1.8.
ECG: sinus tachycardia only.

Management: IV thiamine, symptom-triggered IV lorazepam, fluids, magnesium. Cultures, UA and chest radiograph for fever.

Impression: Delirium tremens, recurrent.
Disposition: Medical ICU.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admission 11/2/2025, discharge 11/7/2025.

Principal: Delirium tremens (third complicated withdrawal in 11 months).
Secondary: Stress hyperglycemia; sinus tachycardia from withdrawal; severe alcohol use disorder; compensated alcoholic cirrhosis; hypertension; thiamine deficiency; MDD; GERD.

Course: ICU for 3 days on symptom-triggered IV lorazepam, which was weaned by day 3, with high-dose IV thiamine, fluids and magnesium. Fever resolved by day 2; chest film clear, UA negative, blood cultures no growth at 5 days. Moved to the medical floor on day 4. Bilirubin 1.8 on admission, attributed to the acute illness on a background of cirrhosis; no encephalopathy. Addiction medicine consulted. This time he says he wants help staying stopped; he and his sister were given referral information for an outpatient program and asked to see primary care promptly to arrange it and discuss anti-craving medication.

Discharge medications (unchanged): thiamine 100 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, multivitamin 1 tab daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.

Follow-up: PCP within one week; hepatology as scheduled.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Five days out from his third withdrawal admission (11/2 to 11/7, DTs again, ICU). Discharge summary and ED record reviewed. Sister came.

Different tone today. He has not had a drink since he went in - now about two weeks counting the three days before - and says he is done: 'I can't do that again.' Cravings are strong in the afternoons. Sleeping badly. No hallucinations, no tremor since discharge. Mood low but hopeful, no SI.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Calm, oriented, no tremor, no asterixis. Anicteric. Abdomen soft, no ascites.

A/P
1. Severe AUD, early abstinence after three complicated withdrawals. He wants treatment. Starting acamprosate 666 mg three times a day (renal function normal on recent labs; BMP today to confirm) - chosen over naltrexone because of the cirrhosis, as hepatology also suggested. Referral placed to an outpatient addiction program; he agreed to group and individual counseling there. Discussed that a slip should not mean stopping cold again - call us.
2. Delirium tremens, resolved.
3. MDD - counseling through the program; still declines an antidepressant.
4. Cirrhosis - next surveillance US in December, hepatology in January.
5. HTN, GERD, thiamine deficiency - unchanged.
See me in 2 months, or sooner if any slip.

documents.body:
Outpatient addiction treatment program - intake summary to referring primary care, intake completed 12/1/2025.

Thank you for referring Mr. Shapiro. He completed intake with our counselor and addiction medicine clinician. He reports no alcohol since late October, confirmed by his sister, who attended. Diagnosis: alcohol use disorder, severe. Co-occurring depressive symptoms noted; he prefers counseling to medication at this time.

Current medications reviewed: acamprosate 666 mg three times daily, thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, multivitamin, omeprazole 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg. Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: intensive outpatient groups three mornings a week for 8 weeks, then weekly individual counseling. Continue acamprosate as prescribed by you. We will send updates if anything changes.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two-month check after starting acamprosate.

No alcohol since the end of October, by his account, and his sister (in the waiting room) backs that up. Finishing the intensive groups at the program this month, then weekly counseling. Taking acamprosate three times a day, misses the midday dose now and then. Some loose stools the first couple of weeks, gone now. Cravings 'a lot less.' Sleep still rough but better. PHQ-9 6, no SI. Still smoking a pack a day; says one thing at a time.

Exam: BP, pulse and weight as charted, weight steady. Alert, bright, no tremor. Anicteric. Abdomen soft, no ascites. No edema.

A/P
- Severe AUD, abstinent ~2.5 months on acamprosate plus program. Real progress, told him so. Continue 666 mg TID.
- Cirrhosis: CMP, CBC, GGT today. Hepatology later this month.
- MDD: improving with counseling; no medication.
- HTN controlled on amlodipine.
- Tobacco: not ready; revisit once sobriety is steadier.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Liver numbers improving
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, Kevin. Your liver enzymes are the best I've seen them: AST 61 (it has sat in the 70s), ALT 45 (around 50 before), GGT 112 (around 150 before). That is your liver responding to not drinking. Blood counts and kidney tests normal. Keep going.

documents.title: Hepatology follow-up
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Outside hepatology group, visit 1/27/2026.

Interval: a third admission for delirium tremens in November 2025, after which he started acamprosate through his primary care physician and joined an outpatient addiction program. He reports complete abstinence since late October. No decompensating events.

Medications: acamprosate 666 mg three times daily, thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, multivitamin, omeprazole 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg. NKDA.
Exam: Anicteric, no asterixis, no ascites, no stigmata of decompensation.
Labs 1/13: AST 61, ALT 45, GGT 112; December ultrasound without focal lesion or ascites.

Assessment: Compensated alcohol-related cirrhosis, Child-Pugh A, now with sustained early abstinence and improving enzymes.
Plan: Continue abstinence and acamprosate. Surveillance ultrasound in June. Repeat variceal screening endoscopy in late 2026 or 2027 if he remains abstinent. Follow-up in 6 to 8 months.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up.

Still not drinking - five and a half months. Weekly counseling at the program, and a peer support meeting on weekends. Acamprosate three times a day, no side effects now. Mood better, PHQ-9 5, no SI. Smoking unchanged at a pack a day; he asked what the options are and I went through them; he wants to wait until summer.

No jaundice, swelling, confusion or bleeding. Heartburn controlled.

Meds: acamprosate 666 mg TID, thiamine 100, folic acid 1, MVI, omeprazole 20, amlodipine 5. NKDA.

Exam: Vitals as charted - BP at goal, weight stable. Well-appearing. No tremor or asterixis. Sclerae anicteric. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites. No edema.

A/P
1. Severe AUD, sustained abstinence on acamprosate with counseling. Continue.
2. Compensated alcoholic cirrhosis - CMP, CBC, INR, GGT, Mg today. Hepatology has the June ultrasound scheduled.
3. HTN - continue amlodipine 5.
4. MDD - improving, continue counseling.
5. GERD, thiamine deficiency - no change.
6. Tobacco - will revisit; he knows to message me when he's ready.
7. Lung CT and FIT due in the fall.
Follow-up in about 5 months, sooner if needed.
